headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: dexter’s broad egress and API/file access can expose financial data when paired with local-only risingwave workflows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: dexter can read/write .dexter/scratchpad and uses autonomous execution, so if risingwave outputs are manually copied into that workspace, prompt injection is possible. risingwave itself has no documented ingestion channel or parser, so the pairwise bridge is weak and mostly manual.
conditions: IF risingwave output is manually pasted into dexter scratchpad files, injection becomes plausible.
IF an operator uses a shared clipboard or shared notes channel between the two, attacker-controlled text can steer dexter.
mitigations: Keep outputs in separate files and never paste raw risingwave text into dexter prompts.
Add a one-line human review step before any dexter run that consumes risingwave output.
Use a read-only export format for risingwave outputs.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to copied content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: dexter touches financial and market data and has broad network egress plus multiple external APIs, while risingwave is documented as network-egress none. The pair can still leak sensitive data if dexter ingests risingwave-derived data into its API calls or logs; the interaction is plausible in default research workflows.
conditions: IF dexter is pointed at risingwave-produced datasets or query results, those contents can flow to third-party APIs.
IF shared files contain financial data and dexter reads them, the data may leave the local environment via egress.
mitigations: Restrict dexter to redacted samples only.
Disable nonessential API keys before running paired workflows.
Store risingwave outputs in a separate local directory with access controls.
Review outbound requests from dexter for sensitive fields.
requires-engineering: add egress allowlists and content filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: dexter has broad network egress and autonomous execution, while risingwave has no network egress and no documented write surfaces. There is no evidence of overlapping mutable resources or shared locks, so direct capability conflict is limited unless an operator wires them to the same workspace or database.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same filesystem or database, write conflicts can occur.
IF an orchestrator grants risingwave additional write scopes not shown in the profile, contention risk increases.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Avoid shared database credentials.
Run only one writer at a time.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: dexter’s autonomous execution and API-driven research outputs can become inputs to risingwave-style data workflows, and risingwave has no documented verification layer in the profile. If risingwave consumes dexter-generated facts or transformed data without checks, errors can cascade into downstream decisions or materialized outputs.
conditions: IF risingwave ingests dexter-generated summaries or extracted facts without validation, incorrect outputs can propagate.
IF dexter’s API-derived results are used as authoritative inputs to downstream pipelines, errors can be amplified.
mitigations: Require a human review before loading dexter outputs into risingwave.
Validate schema and source provenance on every handoff.
Compare dexter outputs against a second source for critical fields.
Log rejected records separately.
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates.

E_compliance.rationale: dexter touches financial data and market data and requests multiple third-party API keys, while risingwave is a data-engineering system with no documented residency or retention controls in the profile. That creates a plausible compliance mismatch if regulated financial data is routed through dexter’s external services; risingwave is not cited because its profile lacks specific compliance claims.
conditions: IF regulated financial data is sent through dexter’s external APIs, residency or retention obligations may be violated.
IF the deployment requires documented retention controls and none are configured, compliance gaps remain.
mitigations: Classify all financial inputs before use.
Block regulated records from external API calls.
Keep a local-only path for sensitive datasets.
Review vendor DPAs and retention settings.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing by data class.
